title: Review classification under repeated wording
question: Does rating-group classification remain useful when repeated wording is excluded?

filtering.deduplication: Earliest answered review per order, before excluding missing comment text.

protocol.target: rating 1–2 negative; rating 3 neutral; rating 4–5 positive
protocol.selection_rule: Maximum validation macro-F1 among the two predeclared text representations; ties follow declaration order. Majority remains an independent reference. No test-driven selection or tuning.
protocol.fit_rule: Vocabulary, IDF, classifier and majority class fitted on the earliest training partition only. No train+validation refit.
protocol.time_rule: First approximately 60% training, next 20% validation, final 20% test by review-answer timestamp; equal timestamps stay together.
protocol.normalization: Unicode NFKD casefold, remove accent marks, retain alphanumeric tokens and collapse punctuation/whitespace. Exact equality after this transform only; near-duplicate and paraphrase detection is not performed.
protocol.test_status: The broader Olist cohort and its final period were inspected in an earlier published benchmark. This is a retrospective diagnostic, not a pristine unseen confirmatory test.

selected_model.name: Character TF-IDF + logistic regression
selected_model.selection_reason: Highest validation macro-F1 among the predeclared learned candidates.

confusion_matrix_axes: Rows: actual; columns: predicted. Both use labels order.

duplicates.normalization: Unicode NFKD casefold, remove accent marks, retain alphanumeric tokens and collapse punctuation/whitespace. Exact equality after this transform only; near-duplicate and paraphrase detection is not performed.

findings: Validation selected Character TF-IDF + logistic regression (macro-F1 0.6693) from two fixed text representations.
On all 8,085 final-period reviews, selected-model macro-F1 was 0.6533; training-majority baseline 0.2717.
1,537 final-period reviews (19.0%) repeated normalized wording from training or validation.
The weakest final-period class was neutral (F1 0.2998, support 669).
After excluding wording seen in earlier partitions, 6,548 reviews remained; macro-F1 was 0.6475, versus baseline 0.2605.
limitations: Retrospective diagnostic: the dataset and final period were already inspected in the earlier public benchmark; this is not untouched evidence of improvement.
Ratings are proxy target groups, not independently annotated sentiment. Identical wording can legitimately have conflicting ratings.
The novel-text subset excludes exact normalized wording seen earlier; it does not remove paraphrases, near duplicates, shared authors or seller effects.
The subset changes the case mix. Its score is a robustness diagnostic, not an unbiased estimate of all future reviews or a causal measure of memorization.
Bootstrap intervals resample normalized-text groups and do not account for temporal drift, label uncertainty, model selection or transfer to other marketplaces.

Two feature sets and fixed classifier settings were selected for a bounded educational ablation. Word/character vocabulary budgets differ; this is not a controlled comparison at equal representation size.
Only earliest answered reviews with eligible comments enter the cohort. Source timezone and ingestion delays are not established.
No raw text, customer/order identifiers or trained vocabulary are included in the public study artifact. This is an offline study; the site displays recorded results.
